First you need an image, I'm going to use this one for the example: https://i.sli.mg/nBRG4I.png

Second you need a website, I'm going to use https://duckduckgo.com

Third you have to add a link to that website on your sidebar, the markdown code for my example would be [DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com) (the text between is important for people with custom CSS disabled).

Once you have added a link on your sidebar you have to use this CSS:

.side { padding-top: 250px; }
@media all and (min-width:871px) { .side { position: relative; } }
.side .md a[href="https://duckduckgo.com"] {
 position: absolute;
 top: 0;
 display: block;
 width: 100%;
 height: 250px;
 font-size: 0;
 background: url(https://i.sli.mg/nBRG4I.png) no-repeat;
 background-size: contain;
 background-position: 50% 50%;
}

Notes: the 250px padding and height will vary depending on the aspect ratio of your image, experiment with different values until it looks right. Change the background URL to a link to the image you want. Change the a[href="..."] link to the link you added to the sidebar.
